builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games
summary: GameDojo replaces ad hoc or non-interactive agent evaluations with a controlled benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 games, plus 600 hours of gameplay trajectories for training and evaluation. Adoption costs include engineering effort to reconstruct and run the environments, compute for real-time rollouts, and, if used for training, fine-tuning a 4B model on the trajectory data. It can fail as a proxy: gains on game bosses may not transfer to business tasks, and models can overfit the benchmark without improving general interactive competence.
rationale: This is a benchmark and dataset contribution for real-time game agents rather than a deployable efficiency or capability technique, so it is worth tracking but offers no immediate production gain on constrained infrastructure.
technique: Real-time gameplay agent benchmark with training data

claims.statement: GameDojo replaces ad hoc or non-interactive agent evaluations with a controlled benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 games, plus 600 hours of gameplay trajectories for training and evaluation. Adoption costs include engineering effort to reconstruct and run the environments, compute for real-time rollouts, and, if used for training, fine-tuning a 4B model on the trajectory data. It can fail as a proxy: gains on game bosses may not transfer to business tasks, and models can overfit the benchmark without improving general interactive competence.

Training on 600 hours of GameDojo-Data brings GameDojo-4B to frontier-level performance on the benchmark with the strongest real-time interaction results; no multiplicative factor over a named baseline is given.
